SAF prices rebounded later in 2025, likely due to the European Union’s ReFuelEU mandate which passed in September 2023 and was implemented in 2025 (Perkins 2023). The European Union reported a 2024 market price of HEFA-based SAF of $6.83/gal (European Union Aviation Safety Agency 2024). Both conventional jet fuel and SAF prices are based on production costs plus additional costs such as distribution, certification, marketing, and margins. Figure 29 includes IATA’s minimum selling price for various SAFs, which includes $3.03/gal added to cover additional costs based on European HEFA SAF (IATA 2024c). IATA defines the minimum selling price as “price at which fuel suppliers will sell SAF to airlines without losing money and allowing them to cover costs of capital” (IATA 2024c). Minimum fuel selling prices are based on covering the following costs: capital, fixed and variable operating, feedstock, and fuel sales tax. Current and future prices paid for SAF are expected to be higher than the minimum fuel selling price plus additional costs shown in Figure 29 (IATA 2024c). IATA HEFA modeled prices increase slightly due to feedstock competition whereas other pathway prices are expected to decline with scaling (IATA 2024c). The U.K. Department for Transport developed SAF production cost assumptions as part of their evaluation of SAF mandate impacts (U.K. Department for Transport 2023). The methodology to develop the costs was based on “bottom-up techno-economic modelling,” including capital and operating expenses for each pathway and feedstock combination. The modeling included low, mid, and high price scenarios, and prices declined for all pathway and feedstock combinations between 2035 and 2050. Additional methodology inputs are available in the referenced report (U.K. Department for Transport 2023).
